summary: TerraPulse is an interactive web platform that shows what is changing in Earth’s environment, where, by how much, and whether the change is statistically significant. Using NASA POWER data for 1990–2024, we processed monthly Temperature and Rainfall at 60 grid points (30 locations per variable), removed the seasonal cycle to get anomalies, and measured trends with the Theil-Sen slope and the Mann-Kendall test, corrected for multiple testing with the Benjamini-Hochberg False Discovery Rate. A FastAPI backend serves the results to a React and Leaflet map where red, blue and grey zones mark significant increase, significant decrease and no significant change, with click-through popups and time-series graphs. The tool reveals opposite regional responses: 13 temperature locations changed significantly (12 warming, one cooling), while only 2 rainfall locations stayed significant after correction. By separating real change from noise, TerraPulse helps people focus on trends that matter.
details:
What we found

13 of 30 temperature locations show significant change after correction: 12 warming and one cooling (Southern Indian Ocean region, about -1.17 °C over 34 years). Rainfall is much noisier: 10 locations looked significant before correction, but only 2 survived it. We also checked the opposite trends against global mean temperature: the warming location follows it closely (r = 0.77), while the cooling location moves against the global trend but still tracks its year-to-year variation (r = 0.40 after removing trends). This is consistent with one global system producing different regional responses. It does not prove causation.

Benefits and impact

Global averages hide regional differences. TerraPulse helps students, researchers and decision-makers see which changes are real and which are likely noise, so attention goes to trends that matter. Reporting only corrected results avoids overstating weak signals.

Tools

Python (Pandas, NumPy, SciPy), FastAPI, Uvicorn, Pydantic, React, Vite, TailwindCSS, Leaflet with CartoDB tiles.

What makes it creative

We built the tool around statistical honesty rather than only visual appeal: significance is shown directly on the map, uncertain locations stay grey, and missing data is flagged separately instead of being hidden.

Factors we considered and limitations

Seasonal bias, missing values, multiple testing, and robustness to outliers. Our grid is coarse (30° spacing), and we did not apply autocorrelation correction (such as Hamed-Rao), which would be the next improvement along with finer resolution and more variables.
dataRefs: NASA POWER (Prediction Of Worldwide Energy Resources) Monthly API
